stemBlocks.value: The variable p varies inversely as q. The table gives q = 4, a, 10 with p = 15, 6, b. (a) Find the equation connecting p and q. (b) Find the value of a. (c) Find the value of b.
Think first: The first column is complete, so start there and let the constant fill in the rest.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p119-q16 from workbook page 119.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the variation statement as an equation.
Use the complete column q = 4, p = 15 to find k.
Find a, the q value that gives p = 6.
Find b, the p value when q = 10.

strategyBlocks.value: Write p = k/q, find k from q = 4, p = 15, then use the equation to find a (a q value) and b (a p value).

whyThisWorks.value: Because pq is constant at 60, the equation can be read in either direction: divide 60 by q to get p, or divide 60 by p to get q. That is why an unknown in the top row and an unknown in the bottom row are handled by the same single relationship.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing q by k instead of k by q when the unknown is in the top row.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing q by k instead of k by q when the unknown is in the top row.
Avoid this: Finding k as 4 ÷ 15 rather than 4 × 15.

commonErrors.misconception: Stopping after part (b) without using the same k for part (c).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Stopping after part (b) without using the same k for part (c).

examTip.value: Write the equation with the value of k substituted before answering the later parts — each part is then a one-line calculation.
